sections.what_happened: NEW CALLED RACES since 0600-02 (which had only governors + early Senate holds): (1) SENATE FLIP — Democrat Roy Cooper wins North Carolina's Republican-held seat, defeating Michael Whatley (AP: NC Called, 90.32% estimated vote; Times/USA Today: first Senate flip of the night). (2) GEORGIA SWEEP — Jon Ossoff (Dem) reelected to Senate (AP: GA Called; NBC/DDHQ projected, 60.49% vs Mike Collins with 130/159 counties reporting) and Keisha Lance Bottoms (Dem) projected Georgia governor (NBC/DDHQ, 55.59% vs Rick Jackson's 44.41% at call), ending 24 years of Republican rule and, per USA Today, making her the first Black woman ever elected governor of a US state. (3) HOLDS/OTHER CALLS — Chris Pappas (Dem) wins New Hampshire Senate (AP: NH Called; first openly gay man elected to the chamber, per Times/USA Today); Mark Warner (Dem) reelected Virginia Senate (AP: VA Called); Ashley Moody (R) reelected Florida Senate (AP: FL Called); Shelley Capito (R) reelected West Virginia Senate (AP: WV Called); Helena Foulkes (Dem) Rhode Island governor (already in 0600-02, confirmed in-window). (4) FLORIDA — Byron Donalds (R) wins governor (Fox call relayed by Times; USA Today: first Black governor of Florida) and Democrat Jamie Ager flips NC-11 House seat (DDHQ/CNN relayed by USA Today) plus a Florida 22nd-district (Mar-a-Lago) Democratic House win (Times). CHAMBER CONTROL STILL UNCALLED: Senate needs net Democratic gain of 4 from a 53-47 Republican start — only 1 confirmed flip (NC) so far; House needs net Democratic gain of 3 — see separate HOLD record 0700-02 for the single-desk DDHQ House projection. AP partial House popular vote at last check: Democrats 30,752,905 vs Republicans 24,803,792, 45.2% estimated, 29.57% precincts reporting — partial, not a result.
sections.what_verified: AP results tables (Called markers for NC, GA, NH, VA, FL, WV Senate) are the primary source for their own calls; governor/House projections rest on NBC/DDHQ relays, which carry no declared tier in the registry and therefore do NOT count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: Chamber control uncalled everywhere checked: Times live says Democrats 'expected to retake the House' but no call; USA Today says Democrats 'made headway' with control unresolved; AP tables still show SC, KS, TX, OH, ME, AK, MI, IA and others 'Too Early to Call'. Georgia's governor result is a projection (NBC/DDHQ), not an AP call in the checked material. Ranked-choice states (Alaska, Maine) and a possible Georgia runoff rule can delay a Senate call for days.
sections.why_matters: The vote that decides what happens next in Iran: Democrats take the first Senate flip and sweep Georgia — lead with Cooper's NC flip + Bottoms' historic win, then the fault line: does a new Congress restrain Trump's 'locked and loaded' Iran option (0600-01) or does war power stay with the White House? Foreign-policy consequence frame only — no horse-race-only video per the proven-topics lock.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW UPDATE TO 0600-02: US midterms (Nov 3) — first Senate flip + Georgia sweep called; chamber control STILL uncalled as of ~07:00

totw_analysis: Our read: The vote that decides what happens next in Iran: Democrats take the first Senate flip and sweep Georgia — lead with Cooper's NC flip + Bottoms' historic win, then the fault line: does a new Congress restrain Trump's 'locked and loaded' Iran option (0600-01) or does war power stay with the White House? Foreign-policy consequence frame only — no horse-race-only video per the proven-topics lock. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Was this a referendum on the Iran war and living costs (fuel prices, tariffs) — or a normal midterm swing that leaves Trump's foreign policy untouched? Manila Times frames the vote as 'a nationwide judgment on Trump's turbulent second term, with discontent over living costs, tariffs and the US war against Iran'; the counter-read is that a House flip alone does not stop a president's war powers.
